question: Can start-of-film context reinstatement and retrieval monitoring, without a maintained category cue, produce selective protection anywhere in their admissible parameter space, and if so is that protection robust or accompanied by a generic increase in film recall?

claim_scope.included: A finite-grid global sensitivity analysis over the complete admissible [0, 1] domains of effective start-of-film drift and rejected-item context carryover, under the fixed fitted eCMR regime used by the manuscript.
claim_scope.excluded: This analysis does not prove a statement over every point in the continuous parameter space, estimate parameters from trauma-film data, quantify uncertainty in the fitted base parameters, or establish psychological plausibility from simulated outcomes alone.

parameter_interpretation.beta_start_effective: Actual drift toward the model's start-of-film temporal context. Zero disables start reinstatement; one replaces the retrieval context completely.
parameter_interpretation.kappa: Proportion of the ordinary retrieved-item context update retained after a sampled non-film item. One disables monitoring; zero is maximal monitoring.

families.description: Isolates the maintained category cue against the unguided baseline.
Adds the category cue to the manuscript's fitted start drift and maximal-monitoring setting.

estimands.notation: Y[c, r, t] is mean film items recalled for retrieval-control configuration c, reminder r, and task strength t.
estimands.task_cost: D[c, r] = Y[c, r, weak] - Y[c, r, strong]
estimands.primary_selective_protection: P[c] = S[unguided] - S[c]. This is the retrieval-control x reminder x task contrast; positive values indicate selective protection relative to no control.
estimands.endpoint_loss: L[c] = Y[c, no_reminder, weak] - Y[c, with_reminder, strong]. This is the low-versus-high contrast displayed in the current control-decomposition figure.
estimands.endpoint_protection: P_endpoint[c] = L[unguided] - L[c]. This secondary descriptive estimand directly tests whether a setting reduces the loss shown in the current decomposition figure, but it does not isolate the reminder-specific selective-interference interaction.
estimands.generic_recall_gain: G[c] = Y[c, no_reminder, weak] - Y[unguided, no_reminder, weak]
estimands.high_interference_gain: H[c] = Y[c, with_reminder, strong] - Y[unguided, with_reminder, strong]
estimands.interpretation_rule: Primary three-way protection, within-reminder protection, endpoint protection, and generic gain are reported separately. A positive secondary contrast cannot be described as reminder-specific selective protection unless the primary three-way contrast is also positive. No weighted score, tuned pass threshold, or post-hoc winner rule is used.

mechanism_diagnostics.start_reinstatement: Film recall probability by input position, including early (1-5), middle (6-11), and late (12-16) summaries.
mechanism_diagnostics.monitoring: Probability that the next nonzero output is a film item conditional on the current output being a non-film item and recall continuing.
mechanism_diagnostics.all_mechanisms: Full film serial-position curves for declared representative settings in the reminder-plus-strong-task condition.

uncertainty.method: Ten independently keyed Monte Carlo batches, reused as common random numbers in every model cell.
uncertainty.interval: Two-sided 95% Student-t interval over paired batch estimands.
uncertainty.scope: Intervals quantify Monte Carlo error only, not empirical sampling error or parameter uncertainty.

selection_policy: All grid points and both comparator curves are retained and reported. The analysis does not select settings by a weighted objective or tune parameters to recreate a target figure.
